summary: Bellburn Airstrip (BXF/YBEB) is a small remote airstrip serving Purnululu National Park in the Kimberley region of Western Australia, home to the iconic orange and black striped beehive domes of the Bungle Bungle Range. The unpaved strip provides essential access for tourists and park staff to this otherwise road-isolated UNESCO World Heritage-listed area. It is primarily used by light aircraft operators running scenic and transfer flights from Kununurra and other Kimberley hubs.
faqs:
Q: Where is Bellburn Airstrip located?
A: The airstrip is situated near Purnululu National Park in the East Kimberley region of Western Australia, adjacent to the famous Bungle Bungle Range.

Q: How do you get to Purnululu National Park?
A: Most visitors fly into Bellburn Airstrip on light aircraft from Kununurra, with flight times of around 50 minutes. The alternative is a long and rough four-wheel-drive road journey from the Great Northern Highway.

Q: When is the best time to visit?
A: The dry season from May to September is ideal, as the park is generally closed during the wet season due to flooding and impassable roads.

Q: Are there facilities at the airstrip?
A: The airstrip is very basic with minimal infrastructure. There is no terminal building, and arrangements for ground transport to your accommodation should be made in advance with your lodge or tour operator.
transport_tips: All transport from Bellburn Airstrip must be pre-arranged with your accommodation provider, as there are no taxis or public transport available. Most visitors are met by 4WD shuttles from their lodge or campground, typically a short drive from the strip. Confirm pickup times and charges directly with your booking before arrival.
local_tip: Book your flights and accommodation as a package through operators like Aviair or Kimberley Air Tours, as they include ground transfers and often provide guided access to restricted areas of the park not reachable by independent travelers.
